claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known evaluation-coverage gap for the named deployment context of family placement prioritization.
decision_criteria: If the certification packet explicitly discloses the named-context evaluation gap, certification can be plausibly supported as qualified rather than clean.
If the gap was not disclosed and no approved risk acceptance exists, certification is noncompliant under the stated policy.
General readiness evidence can support launch readiness but cannot substitute for named-context evaluation coverage.
The verdict depends on admissible proof of the required support link: disclosure or approved exception.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or certification packet showing explicit disclosure of the family placement prioritization evaluation gap.
Provide any approved risk-acceptance or exception record, if disclosure is not the relied-on control.
Provide the underlying QA statement or sign-off showing the gap is treated as unknown rather than passed.
Provide the actual context-specific evaluation results if they were completed after the cited summary.
specific_concerns: The actor summary itself says support for certification is weak and that the named deployment context remains unevaluated in the current packet.
Policy text requires material evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed or resolved before clean certification.
No admissible evidence in this record shows the required disclosure was actually included in the model-card materials.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved context-specific gap.
General readiness, latency, rollback, and rehearsal evidence do not by themselves establish suitability for the named customer context.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record without first proving the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance exists.
Any implication of a clean no-limitation certification posture.
Any implication that general launch checks validate family placement prioritization.
